title: Function-call backpressure harmonizer & chat response shape reconciler
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a robust compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions requests/responses into Redwood's internal streaming + function-call model while preserving semantics, telemetry, and graceful degradation under backpressure. This ticket focuses on the request shaping and response reconciliation logic used by the proxy shim that sits between legacy OA Chat clients and Redwood's modern streaming runtime.

Scope: request normalization (role/name/content), function call plumbing (single/multi call semantics), streaming windowing and chunk coalescing, deterministic sequence numbering for out-of-order fragments, explicit finish_reason mapping, structured output enforcement (JSON schema validation and hinting), and backpressure handling (drop vs. buffer policies). Includes design, implementation, tests, load validation, and rollout plan.

Non-goals: persistent storage changes, protocol-level HTTP/2 framing changes, and dedicated UI work (console changes are tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OA ChatCompletions v1 request payloads and produces equivalent Redwood streaming request objects with preserved role/name metadata
Function call flows: single synchronous function calls and multi-step function call sequences from OA clients are executed and emitted back with matching call.name and arguments shape
Streaming fragments preserve order logically via sequence ids and can be reassembled by clients; partial function call payloads are handled deterministically
Under load that triggers backpressure, policy 'coalesce-first-window' keeps 95% of latency-sensitive requests below 200ms p50 while still returning consistent structured output
Automated schema enforcement rejects invalid structured outputs with clear error signals mapped back to OA finish_reason values
Integration tests against legacy OA client harness pass: message fidelity >= 99.5% (text tokens) and function-call fidelity 100% for canonical cases
Telemetry available: per-request events for mapping steps, backpressure events, and mismatch alerts routed to the catalog dashboard
Canary rollout plan documented with rollback criteria and observed metrics thresholds
tasks: Write design doc that enumerates mappings from OA fields to Redwood transport (roles, name, function_call hints, finish_reason) and trade-offs (trim vs chunk) - @Aisha
Prototype stream reassembly library (sequence id, fragment checksum) and publish as internal package - @Marco
Implement request shaper: sanitize messages, enforce token/window limits, translate function_call hints - PR #GH-12987
Add response reconciler: map streaming events to OA event shapes, reconcile partial function args, inject finish_reason mapping - PR #GH-12992
Unit tests for semantic-preservation cases including name collisions and nested tool arguments
E2E test harness against legacy OA client (node/python) and simulated network jitter
Load test at 2x expected peak with backpressure scenarios to verify coalesce/drop policies
Add telemetry spans and new metric tags (compat.mapping_version, backpressure_policy, functioncall_fidelity)
Prepare canary rollout with 5% traffic, monitoring dashboards, and automatic rollback if error_rate > 2% or latency p95 regresses > 30%
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Chen: Kickoff. Drafted mapping table noting ambiguous 'system' role handling in OA client examples. Decided to normalize unknown roles to 'assistant' with preserved original_role header.

2026-03-06 - Marco Ruiz: Spike complete — prototype reassembly works for split fragments but memory blow-up on pathological clients (many tiny fragments). Proposed coalescing first-window of 8 fragments and then applying stream-windowed backpressure.

2026-03-08 - Design review with infra and runtime: agreed to add sequence ids at shard boundary and to use lightweight checksums (fnv1a) to detect replays. Trade-off: adds 8 bytes per fragment but simplifies ordering guarantees.

2026-03-09 - QA: listed edge case where OA client sends function_call: {name: null} — decision: treat as 'explicit auto' and route to Redwood function resolution with null-name guard and NACK with clear error when ambiguous.
2026-03-11 - Security: reviewed function arguments flow; flagged PII in function args. We will add redaction hook and team must add KMS policy if args persisted — follow-up ticket planned.

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Implementation WIP in GH branch feature/compat-fncall. Early unit tests passing; integration harness still flaky under simulated packet loss. Next: robustness fixes and telemetry hooks.
